Hi Rajeev,

RRO doesn't have a explicit dependency on Java itself. RRO will only install those system libraries
that are a dependency required for base R itself. That is why we don't install libicu by default.


Stephen Weller
RRO Technical Support Engineer

On Thursday, September 17, 2015 at 1:53:19 PM UTC-7, Rajeev Vij wrote:
Hi Stephen, Thanks for the note. yes this help resolve rJava issue. I am able to install it.

In fact the missing package was "libicu-devel.x86_64" the package "libicu.x86_64" was already installed.
My question why does RRO-3.2.2 not install all the dependent linux packages during installation.

Does RRO-3.2.2 assume that base package is already installed and have all the dependent libraries available and then install RRO-3.2.2?


On Thursday, September 17, 2015 at 8:20:19 AM UTC-7, Stephen Weller wrote:
The installation is failing because it can't find a system library.
It looks like you are missing the 'libicu' library, which is a system dependency for base R.

Try this on the machine with RRO 3.2.2 installed on it:

%yum install libicu


Then try reinstalling the rJava package.

Revolution R Open Technical Support
